verdict.rationale: Statsig documents a Console API described as a CRUD API for doing console actions without the web UI. It also ships an official MCP server for agent tools like Codex, Cursor and Claude Code, and feature gates are documented as toggleable in real time. So an agent can plausibly create and toggle flags programmatically, but the evidence never explicitly shows gate creation, targeting-rule edits, or which write operations the MCP server exposes. missing for 10: explicit docs for creating and targeting gates via Console API, documented MCP write tools for flag create/target/toggle, independent or hands-on corroboration, a published OpenAPI spec (probe found none).

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent create, target, and toggle feature flags through the API or MCP server

citations.quote: The Console API is the CRUD API for performing the actions available on console.statsig.com without using the web UI.
The Statsig MCP (Model Context Protocol) server brings the power of Statsig into tools like Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code.
Feature Gates, commonly known as feature flags, allow you to toggle the behavior of your product in real time without deploying new code.
